output.methodChoice: Collected X15 only (most discriminating item for supervision/workload vs market explanations). Stopped at one item because supervising partner and Kestrel workload are fully confounded in the records, so a second record is unlikely to separate them.
output.brief: What is going on: the departures are concentrated in the group and in the people who worked on Kestrel. 8 of the 11 Kestrel associates resigned, against 1 of the 13 others, and all 11 reported to Dorian Faulk. Other groups' attrition is flat, and the billable-hours rise applied to everyone, so the firm-wide explanations look weak. The records cannot separate Faulk's supervision from the heavy workload: they are the same people and the same matter, and Kestrel places went to the least-utilised associates. Pay is unproven, since no pay comparison has been checked against leavers' stated reasons. Confidence that the problem is specific to Kestrel is fairly high; confidence about whether supervision or workload is the cause is low. What to do next: do not announce the £12k group-wide payment or close the review; it would spend money on the wrong cause and end the inquiry. Commission the confidential interviews, designed to separate how associates experienced supervision from how they experienced workload, before choosing between moving supervision and adding reviewers. Meanwhile, start recording matter and supervising partner in attrition data.
